problems.title: Expand a linear equation
problems.question: Solve 8−5(3x−7)=1−4(x+17).
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
steps: Add 15x and 67 to both sides:110=11x. Divide by 11. Check: the original left and right sides both equal −107.

problems.title: Three points on a line
problems.question: A, B, C are collinear, BC=3AB and BC−AB=20 cm. Find every possible AC.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
steps: Thus AB=10 and BC=30. If A and C are on opposite sides of B, AC=10+30=40. If they are on the same side of B, AC=30−10=20. These exhaust the positions of A and C relative to B.

problems.title: Evaluate a custom operation
problems.question: $a\otimes b=(a+b)/|b-a|$. Evaluate $3.\overline6\otimes(-14\tfrac23)$.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
steps: The numerator is 11/3−44/3=−11. The denominator is|−44/3−11/3|=55/3. Divide:−11·3/55.

problems.title: Bisectors inside a straight angle
problems.question: Rays OM, ON divide straight angle AOB in that order from OA, into parts inversely proportional to 1,2,6. Find the angle between the bisectors of AOM and NOB.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
formulas: The parts have ratio $1:1/2:1/6=6:3:1$ and sum 180°.
steps: Each ratio unit is 18°, so AOM=108°, MON=54°, NOB=18°. The first bisector is 54° from OA. The last is 108°+54°+9°=171° from OA. Subtract.

problems.title: Find the initial advertisement count
problems.question: A company sells one third of its advertisements and then 12 more. The remainder is 6 less than half the initial number. Find the initial count.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
formulas: If the initial count is N, $2N/3-12=N/2-6$.
steps: Subtract N/2 and add 12: N/6=6. Thus N=36. Check:36−12−12=12, also 36/2−6=12.

problems.title: Five angles from a parallel-line diagram
problems.question: Two parallel lines meet a transversal. Five of the eight angles sum to 549°. Find the larger angle.
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
formulas: The eight angles consist of four α and four $(180°-α)$. If k of the chosen five equal α, then $kα+(5-k)(180-α)=549$, where $k=1,2,3,4$.
steps: For k=1,2,3,4 the equation gives α=57°,−9°,189°,123°, respectively. Only 57° and 123° are valid, and they describe the same pair of supplementary angles. Hence the larger is 123°. Check:4·123+57=549.

problems.title: Time lost before starting work
problems.question: A builder was allotted 5 hours. Starting late, they do the first third at 25% above the planned rate, then reduce that increased rate by 20% and finish on time. How late did they start?
problems.idea: Write the conditions as equations and keep every possible case.
formulas: The planned rate is $1/5$ job/hour. The increased rate is $(5/4)(1/5)=1/4$; after the reduction it is $(4/5)(1/4)=1/5$.
steps: Time for the first third is(1/3)/(1/4)=4/3 hours. Time for the remaining two thirds is(2/3)/(1/5)=10/3 hours. Total working time is 14/3 hours=4 hours 40 minutes. The allotted 5 hours leave 20 minutes before work began.
